subject: FinBridge deployment preference & hosted quickstart follow-up
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@finbridge.com>, Alyssa Kent <alyssa.kent@finbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 3:10 PM -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up and next steps from today's demo

Hi Sam / Alyssa — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple asks so we can scope the right evaluation lane (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):

- Summary: You ran the demo of the checkout fraud scoring flow and liked inference latency/quality on the M+ model. Primary constraints: PCI-adjacent data (no PHI), ~2M inference calls/month forecast for Q4 if pilot looks good, and a desire to avoid large infra ops overhead.

As discussed, next items we can action from our side:
1) Hosted evaluation sandbox: we can provision a hosted sandbox with a mirrored endpoint set. Please confirm which endpoints you want ("fraud-score-v1" and/or "batch-scoring" noted).
2) Rate/throughput targets: call out any concurrency or per-minute target (we typically set trial defaults but can raise limits for the sandbox).
3) Security/compliance materials: attaching a SOC2 summary and a short sandbox access instructions file. If you need the full SOC2 report or a network egress diagram, we can route through your procurement security contact.
4) Dedicated/Private appetite: if you expect sustained throughput >10M calls/mo or strict network isolation, we can draft a Dedicated capacity estimate or Private VPC package. Marissa will own pricing.

Deliverable timeline: SE (Diego) can configure the sandbox and send credentials within 48 business hours after we get the endpoint list + target rate. Marissa will follow up on preferred contract cadence if you want to discuss reserved capacity.

Can you confirm: endpoints to enable, desired request/min and concurrency, and whether we should send the full SOC2 report to procurement?

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf (summary), sandbox-instructions.txt (how to use the hosted sandbox)

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — great session. A few clarifying points from our side before you spin up anything: 

- Endpoints: please enable both fraud-score-v1 (sync single-call) and batch-scoring (async batch calls).
- Rate targets for sandbox: we'd like to validate at 100 requests/min for fraud-score-v1 and a batch throughput of ~300 records/min. For concurrency, assume short-lived concurrency up to 10 concurrent calls.
- Token billing: can you confirm token counting for the scoring endpoint (we send short payloads but may include small context windows per request)?
- Compliance: please send the full SOC2 to procurement@finbridge.com, and include any network egress/IP ranges we need to whitelist.

Also — what are your default hosted trial limits? We want to ensure the sandbox isn't bottlenecked below the numbers above.

Sam Patel
Head of Engineering, FinBridge
sam@finbridge.com

On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 3:10 PM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> 
> Quick recap and a couple asks so we can scope the right evaluation lane...

Hi Sam — thanks for the details. Quick answers and what I'll configure for the hosted sandbox: 

- Endpoints: will provision fraud-score-v1 (sync) and batch-scoring (async) as requested. Sandbox endpoints: https://sandbox.redwood.com/finbridge/fraud-score-v1 and https://sandbox.redwood.com/finbridge/batch-scoring (credentials will be API key scoped to those endpoints).
- Rate limits (hosted trial defaults): 60 requests/min per endpoint and burst to 120 for short periods. We can raise the sandbox to 100 req/min for fraud-score-v1 and allow batch throughput ~300 records/min as a trial config — I will request that increase now.
- Concurrency: sandbox will support your stated 10 concurrent calls without queueing; we'll monitor headroom.
- Token counting: Redwood bills per output + input token usage. For scoring, very small context windows are typically 5–15 tokens per request; we'll provide an estimated token/sample after you share a sample payload.
- Network egress/IPs: attaching a CIDR list and egress notes in a separate doc (I'll send to procurement path). If you need a dedicated VPC, we can discuss Private deployment options.

Next steps (I'll action):
1) Provision sandbox endpoints + API key (target: within 48 business hours once Soojin confirms we should proceed).
2) Open an internal ticket to bump the sandbox rate limits to the requested numbers.
3) Share token-per-sample estimate after you drop one JSON example payload (10–50 items is fine).

Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
